summary: A Neighborhood Stories article (September 15, 2023) profiling two local residents who changed careers: Michael Chen, a former financial analyst now moving into data science, and Sarah Gomez, a former marketing manager training for healthcare. It covers their motivations, reskilling, finances, emotional struggles and setbacks, and current progress. Experts Julia Ramirez and Dr. Alex Park place their stories in broader workforce and societal trends.
one_line: Two neighbors, Michael Chen and Sarah Gomez, share their mid-career pivots into data science and healthcare, with expert commentary on shifting careers.
key_facts: Michael Chen is a 45-year-old former financial analyst who moved into the data science industry.
Sarah Gomez is a 35-year-old ex-marketing manager who moved toward healthcare, wanting her work to 'contribute directly to the wellbeing of others'.
Chen started a full-time data science bootcamp on October 1, 2023.
Gomez is taking online courses to become a certified nursing assistant while volunteering at local clinics.
Chen found it difficult being the oldest in the class or not catching on as quickly.
Gomez set a meticulous budget and dipped into savings to fund her career switch; she said 'It's not just a career change; it's a lifestyle change'.
Chen switched to part-time work to accommodate his studies.
Both Chen and Gomez found support in groups of like-minded career changers, which offered emotional support, networking and advice.
Gomez was passed over for a position she felt perfect for, which led her to seek additional certifications that made her a stronger candidate.
Chen has landed a junior data analyst role with a startup.
Gomez is weeks away from her certification exam and already has a job lined up at a local hospital.
Career coach Julia Ramirez said employers value diverse experiences and that skills from one industry can transfer to another.
Sociologist Dr. Alex Park said career fluidity reflects broader societal shifts toward fulfillment and work-life balance.
